subject: angol
title: Is space exploration worth it?
instructionsHu: Vitatkozz a vizsgáztatóval az alábbi állításról. A kiosztott álláspontod: az állítás ELLEN érvelsz (szerinted megéri az űrkutatás) – ezt az álláspontot a vita során nem változtathatod meg. Fejtsd ki az érveidet, reagálj a vizsgáztató ellenérveire, és próbáld meggyőzni őt.

debate.statement: Space exploration is a waste of money that should be spent on solving problems on Earth
candidateIdeas: Many everyday technologies, such as GPS, weather forecasts and satellite communication, come from space research.
Satellites help us to monitor climate change, natural disasters and harvests.
Space budgets are small compared with what countries spend on many other things.
Space exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering.
In the long term, humanity may need resources or places to live beyond Earth.
examinerArguments: Millions of people still don't have clean water, enough food or basic health care.
Sending people to Mars is mainly about national pride and the egos of billionaires.
The money could be used directly to fight climate change.
Rockets and space debris pollute the atmosphere and the space around Earth.
Robots and telescopes can explore space much more cheaply than human missions.

followUpQuestions: How can we justify spending billions on rockets when people are starving?
Hungary sent its second astronaut to the International Space Station in 2025. Was that money well spent?
Wouldn't it be better to spend the money on fighting climate change?

usefulPhrases.en: It has led to inventions such as ...
a tiny fraction of the budget
It's not a question of either ... or ...
usefulPhrases.hu: Nem az a kérdés, hogy vagy ..., vagy ...

usefulPhrases.en: You have a point there, but ...

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Let's discuss this statement: 'Space exploration is a waste of money that should be spent on solving problems on Earth.' What's your view?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I'd strongly disagree. Many technologies we use every day, like GPS, weather forecasts and satellite communication, come directly from space research. Satellites also help us to monitor climate change, natural disasters and harvests, so space research actually helps to solve problems on Earth. And compared with what countries spend on many other things, space budgets are surprisingly small.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: How can we justify spending billions on rockets when people are starving?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I understand why people feel that way. But hunger isn't caused by money spent on rockets – it's mostly a question of politics, wars and distribution. If we stopped all space programmes tomorrow, I doubt that a single extra person would be fed.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Hungary sent its second astronaut to the International Space Station in 2025. Was that money well spent?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think it was. The mission inspired a lot of young people to study science and engineering – several of my classmates followed it every day, and one of them now wants to become an aerospace engineer. Hungarian researchers also prepared experiments for it, so it was an investment in our own research.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Wouldn't it be better to spend the money on fighting climate change?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We should certainly spend more on that, but it isn't either-or. Without satellite data, we wouldn't even know how fast the ice is melting. I'd accept that expensive human missions to Mars could wait, but space research as a whole is far too useful to abandon.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a vizsgázó következetesen az állítás ellen érvel (GPS, időjárás-előrejelzés, műholdas klímamegfigyelés, kis költségvetés), az éhezésre hivatkozó ellenérvre megértéssel, de logikusan reagál, a magyar űrhajós kapcsán személyes példát hoz, a végén pedig részleges engedménnyel (az emberes Mars-utazás várhat) keres kompromisszumot.

Szókincs: pontos tudományos-műszaki szavak (satellite communication, monitor, aerospace engineer, satellite data) és vitafordulatok (I understand why people feel that way; it isn't either-or; I'd accept that …).

Nyelvhelyesség: feltételes mondatok (If we stopped all space programmes tomorrow, I doubt …; Without satellite data, we wouldn't …), szenvedő szerkezet (isn't caused by, would be fed) és a 'far too useful to abandon' szerkezet – hibátlanul.
Érdemes megtanulni: „I understand why people feel that way”, „it isn't either-or”, „an investment in our own research”, „far too useful to abandon”.
